name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 12 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Rick Larsen has a large fundraising edge and no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Larsen near certain to win
No public polling or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Larsen combines a 12-point Democratic district lean, incumbency, and a roughly $2 million warhead against a Republican challenger with no reported fundraising or outside support, while markets price his win probability near 97%. The fundamentals point to a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending for Feller or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 2nd District sits comfortably in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of about 12 points toward the party. Rick Larsen, the longtime incumbent, is running for another term and has raised more than $2 million with $650,000 on hand, while Republican challenger Edwin Feller shows no reported fundraising and no outside groups backing him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast leans on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Larsen near certain. The expected margin is in the low twenties, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
